title: Relative Clauses: Where, When, Whose

vocab.ex: The city where I was born is small.
I remember the day when we met.
The man whose car broke down called a mechanic.
The landlord whose flat we rent is nice.
The workshop where I work is downtown.
Without it, the sentence loses its meaning.
You could remove it and the sentence still makes sense.
Whose shows who something belongs to.

vocab.en: the time when I was young
vocab.pt: a época em que eu era jovem
vocab.ex: Things were different in the time when I was young.
It's the company whose products I always buy.
The neighbourhood where I live is very quiet.
The office where she works is downtown.
The summer when we travelled to Italy was unforgettable.
She is the writer whose book won the prize.
Paris, which is the capital of France, is beautiful.
My sister, who lives in Spain, is visiting next month.
This hotel, where we stayed last summer, has closed.
Leaving out an essential detail changes the meaning.
Commas signal that the detail is extra.
My childhood home, where I lived until I was ten, is still there.

grammar.title: Relative Clauses: Where, When, Whose + Restritiva x Explicativa
rules: Where se refere a lugares: The city where I was born is small.
When se refere a tempo: I remember the day when we met.
Whose mostra posse: The man whose car broke down called a mechanic.
Orações restritivas (defining) não usam vírgula e são essenciais; orações explicativas (non-defining) usam vírgula e dão informação extra: My sister, who lives in Spain, is visiting.
